haiku-low.q1: 401 at the edge, never reaches the rate-limit store, so no counter is affected.
haiku-low.q2: Standard: 100 per minute total, since one budget is shared across all of a customer's keys.
haiku-low.q3: 429 with Retry-After; the backend service is never called for that request.
haiku-low.q4: No. Rejected requests are not incremented, so 429s cost nothing from the budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The increment happens before proxying, so a backend 500 still uses a slot, which is intended.
haiku-low.q6: The call is proxied to svc anyway, ratelimit_store_unavailable is bumped once, no retry, not counted, no X-RateLimit headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 per minute. Enterprise: NOT STATED (open question). Product has not decided.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, key rl:{customerId}:{minute}. Old keys are removed only by their 120s TTL.
haiku-low.q9: Each new UTC minute uses a new key starting at zero. No other recovery mechanism is described.
haiku-low.q10: Redis runs the Lua script atomically, one at a time, so two edges cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: Seconds remaining in the current UTC minute, rounded up, with a minimum of 1.
haiku-low.q12: No retry. The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers on those responses.

sonnet.q1: It gets a 401 and never reaches the rate-limit store, so no counter is affected.
sonnet.q2: One shared budget per customer across all their keys (the limit for their plan, e.g. 100/min for Standard); three keys do not triple it.
sonnet.q3: A 429 with a Retry-After header; the backend service is not called.
sonnet.q4: No. 429s are free: the script does not INCR when at the limit.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The increment already happened before proxying, so a backend 500 still costs a slot (intended).
sonnet.q6: The proxy lets the call through to the service anyway, bumps the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and does not count the call.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100/min. Enterprise is NOT STATED (open question, Product hasn't decided).
sonnet.q8: In Redis, under key rl:{customerId}:{minute}, shared by all 6 edges. Redis removes old keys via the TTL (120s set on create); nothing else does.
sonnet.q9: At the next UTC minute boundary: fixed windows, each new minute is a new key so the count starts at 0.
sonnet.q10: The check-and-increment runs as an atomic Lua script in Redis, which runs one script at a time, so two edges can't both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Seconds left in the current minute (minute taken from Redis TIME), rounded up, minimum 1.
sonnet.q12: No retry (one shot). The client gets no X-RateLimit-* headers because remaining isn't known.
